financials.key_finding:
Credo Technology's financial profile has undergone a near-complete metamorphosis in a compressed 24-month window. In fiscal year 2023 (ended April 2023) the company generated $184 million in revenue while sustaining an operating loss; by the trailing twelve months ended January 2026, revenue had grown to approximately $1.07 billion with GAAP operating income of $323 million and a net profit margin above 30 percent. The inflection was driven by the ramp of HiWire AEC products at hyperscaler accounts: product revenue grew from $165 million in FY2024 to $424 million in FY2025 — a 157 percent increase — and continued accelerating into FY2026 with consecutive quarterly records of $223 million (Q1), $268 million (Q2), and $407 million (Q3).

Non-GAAP gross margins have consistently held in the 67–69 percent band, a level more comparable to pure IP companies than to typical fabless hardware vendors, reflecting Credo's proprietary SerDes architecture and the absence of commodity bill-of-materials exposure. The Q3 FY2026 non-GAAP gross margin of 68.6 percent is the high-water mark to date. Management guided Q4 FY2026 gross margins of 64–66 percent on GAAP and non-GAAP bases, flagging that product mix shifts — particularly the ramp of the 800G optical DSP at lower initial yields — and DustPhotonics integration costs will pressure near-term margins before scale economics improve them.

The balance sheet is fortress-grade for a company of this size: as of Q3 FY2026, cash and short-term investments stood at approximately $1.3 billion against total debt of only $16 million, a net-cash position of roughly $1.29 billion or $6.97 per diluted share. The $750 million cash component of the DustPhotonics acquisition will substantially reduce this cushion; pro-forma net cash after close would be approximately $550 million, still adequate but meaningfully constraining a second large deal without capital markets access. Weighted-average diluted shares outstanding were approximately 197 million in Q3 FY2026, with the 0.92 million shares issued for DustPhotonics representing modest dilution. R&D expenditure in FY2025 was approximately $146 million (33 percent of revenue), consistent with the company's engineering-first culture and the need to fund 224G and beyond SerDes development, optical DSP, and ZeroFlap AEC programs simultaneously.
structural_observations: Revenue base has scaled from $59M in FY2021 to a $1.6B+ annualised run rate by Q3 FY2026, representing a five-year CAGR exceeding 90 percent — an extraordinary but increasingly lapped growth rate that will mechanically compress reported YoY comparisons beginning in FY2027 as Q1–Q2 FY2026 become the base period.

Fiscal year runs on a 52/53-week calendar ending in late April or early May, creating a quarter offset from calendar-year peers; investors must align FY designations carefully: Credo's FY2025 ended May 3, 2025, and its FY2026 will end approximately April–May 2026, making FY2026 Q4 guidance ($425–$435 million) the cleanest near-term financial benchmark.

Gross margin progression is structurally positive: non-GAAP gross margin expanded from 57.6 percent in FY2023 to 61.9 percent in FY2024, 64.8 percent in FY2025, and 68.6 percent in Q3 FY2026, driven by AEC scale, SerDes IP royalty mix, and modest ASP improvement as product sophistication increases; management guidance of 64–66 percent for Q4 FY2026 reflects temporary new-product ramp dynamics, not structural deterioration.

Capital structure is essentially equity-financed with minimal financial leverage: $16 million in total debt against $1.3 billion in cash as of Q3 FY2026 yields a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.01; the DustPhotonics $750 million cash payment will consume most of this buffer and may prompt a secondary offering or credit facility negotiation in fiscal 2027.

Customer concentration creates revenue volatility risk: Amazon Web Services represented 86 percent of product revenue in an earlier quarter and approximately 39 percent by Q3 FY2026 as diversification progressed; the high absolute dependency on two or three hyperscalers means any inventory normalisation cycle or competitive displacement at a single account translates directly into quarter-on-quarter revenue swings potentially exceeding 20 percent.

Peer-group comparison: on a forward EV/Sales basis, CRDO trades at approximately 21x FY2026 consensus revenue versus Marvell (MRVL) at roughly 12–14x and Broadcom (AVGO) at roughly 9–11x forward revenue — a significant premium attributable to CRDO's higher growth rate (85 percent FY2026 YoY versus low-double-digit to mid-teens for peers) but also implying that any guidance cut would carry outsized downside multiple compression.

Market capitalisation volatility has been extreme: CRDO IPO'd at $14 per share in January 2022, fell to single digits during the 2022 semiconductor bear market, and had recovered to approximately $220 per share by late May 2026, representing a roughly 15-fold increase from IPO and placing the company at approximately $40 billion market capitalisation — a valuation that compresses to roughly $22–25 billion under bear-case revenue scenarios showing FY2028 growth normalising to 20–25 percent.

leadership.key_finding:
William J. (Bill) Brennan is the architect of Credo's transformation. He joined as CEO in September 2014, when the company was a single-digit-million-dollar IP licensor with no product revenue. Over the subsequent decade he assembled the engineering team, secured institutional capital culminating in the $100 million BlackRock-led Series D in March 2020, shepherded the January 2022 Nasdaq IPO at $14 per share, and executed the product pivot that took AEC revenue from negligible to a $1.6 billion-plus annualised run rate. Brennan holds the Chairman title in addition to President and CEO, giving him full board authority over strategic direction. He has more than 25 years of semiconductor industry experience and has demonstrated a consistent disposition toward disciplined capital allocation — avoiding acquisitions during the IP era and waiting until the company had sufficient cash to deploy $750 million for DustPhotonics without tapping equity markets. His external governance footprint expanded in 2025 when he joined both the Global Semiconductor Alliance board in July and the Axiado board in November, signalling industry-peer recognition of Credo's growing stature.

Daniel Fleming serves as Chief Financial Officer, having been identified in the fiscal 2025 proxy as the proxy representative alongside Chief Legal Officer James Laufman — a governance detail indicating their operational centrality. Fleming oversees a balance sheet that as of Q3 FY2026 held $1.3 billion in cash against $16 million in debt, and he has guided investor communication through the hyper-growth phase with a notably conservative forecasting posture: management has consistently provided guidance below eventual actuals, building a beat-and-raise narrative that has supported the stock's multiple expansion. The management team's average tenure is approximately 6.2 years, and the board of directors' average tenure is approximately 4.6 years, both consistent with a company in its mid-growth phase that has retained its founding engineering culture. There is no known private-equity sponsor or strategic investor with a controlling position post-IPO; pre-IPO investors Walden International, Celesta Capital, and BlackRock held positions that have been substantially diluted or sold in the public markets.
